1.note:
# General Information:

Ezekiel reports a message that God gives him.

This is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 3:16. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke this message] or [Yahweh spoke these words]

2.note: God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. Alternate translation: [Mortal person] or [Human]

2.q: present a riddle and speak a parable
2.note: Alternate translation: [give them a puzzle to think about] or [tell this story as an illustration]

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelite people group]

3.note: “the ends of its wings were long and full of feathers.” The word “pinion” means the outer end of the wings.
The eagle’s feathers were many different colors.

4.q: It broke off the tips of the branches
4.note: Alternate translation: [It broke off the highest part of the tree]
Alternate translation: [took the top of the tree] or [took the branches]

4.q: he planted it in a city of merchants
4.note: “he planted it in a city that had many merchants.” A merchant is a person who sells things.

5.note:
# General Information:

This is a continuation of the parable about the eagle.
The word “he” is the eagle in the parable.

5.q: He placed it beside a large body of water
5.note: Alternate translation: [the eagle planted the seed in a place where there was a lot of water]

Willow trees grow in places where there is a lot of water. If the eagle planted the seed like a willow, it means that he planted it in a place with a lot of water. Alternate translation: [and planted the seed like one would plant a willow tree by water]

6.note: Alternate translation: [Then the seed began to grow into a plant]

6.q: a spreading vine low to the ground
6.note: Alternate translation: [a vine that spreads out on the ground]
The branches of the vine turned toward the eagle. This means that they began to grow upward towards the sky.
This could mean: (1) “its roots grew under itself into the ground” or (2) “the roots of the vine grew under the eagle.”
Alternate translation: [That is how the vine grew]

6.q: produced branches and sent out shoots
6.note: Alternate translation: [grew branches and spread its shoots]

7.note:
# General Information:

The introductory “but” shows that a different eagle is being described other than the one before.
The word “behold” here alerts us to pay attention to the surprising information that follows.

7.q: This vine turned its roots toward the eagle
7.note: Yahweh speaks of the vine as if it were able to behave like a person and intentionally turned its roots toward the other eagle to receive nourishment from it. Alternate translation: [The roots of the vine grew toward the eagle]

7.q: from the place it had been planted so it would be watered
7.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [from the place that the first eagle had planted it so that it would have water]

8.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [The first eagle had planted the vine]

9.note: Yahweh asks this as a leading question to emphasize the negative answer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [It will not prosper.]

9.q: Will it not be uprooted and stripped of its fruit so that it withers, and all its fresh growth will wither?
9.note: Yahweh asks this rhetorical question to emphasize that the vine will certainly be judged. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. It can also be stated in active form. Alternate translation: [Someone will pull up its roots and pluck out its fruit so all of its growth of leaves will wither away.] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

9.q: No strong arm or many people will be needed to pull it out
9.note: The phrase “strong arm” represents a strong person. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [There will be no need for a strong person or many people to pull it out] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

10.note: Alternate translation: [look] or [listen] or [pay attention to what I am about to tell you]

Yahweh asks this as a leading question to emphasize the negative answer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [It will not grow.]

10.q: Will it not wither when the eastern wind touches it?
10.note: Yahweh asks this rhetorical question to emphasize that this will certainly happen. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [It will wither when the eastern wind touches it.]

10.q: when the eastern wind touches it
10.note: Alternate translation: [when the eastern wind blows on it]

11.note: This is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 3:16. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke this message] or [Yahweh spoke these words]

12.note: This is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 2:5. Alternate translation: [the rebellious people]

12.q: Do you not know what these things mean?
12.note: Yahweh asks this as a leading question in order to provide the answer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [This is what these things mean.]
Alternate translation: [Look] or [Listen] or [Pay attention to what I am about to tell you]

13.note: Alternate translation: [made him swear an oath]

14.q: so the kingdom might become lowly and not lift itself up
14.note: The kingdom being small and weak is spoken of as if it were lowly and being large and powerful as if it lifted itself up. Alternate translation: [so the kingdom might remain small and not become great]
Here the word “land” represents the kingdom of Judah and the people in it. Alternate translation: [the kingdom will continue to exist]

15.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh speaks about the king of Jerusalem rebelling against the king of Babylon.

Yahweh asks this leading question to emphasize the negative answer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [He will certainly not succeed.]

15.q: Will the one doing these things escape?
15.note: Yahweh asks this leading question to emphasize the negative answer. This may be translated as a statement. Alternate translation: [The one doing these things will not escape.]

15.q: If he breaks the covenant, will he escape?
15.note: Yahweh asks this leading question to emphasize the negative answer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [If he breaks the covenant, he will certainly not escape.]

16.q: the land of the king who made him king, the king whose oath he despised
16.note: Alternate translation: [the land of the king of Babylon who made him King of Judah, the king of Babylon whose oath he despised]

17.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh speaking about the king of Jerusalem.

17.q: his mighty army and a great company of men
17.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing and emphasize how large and strong Pharaoh’s army is.
Here the word “him” refers to the king of Judah.
this refers to a tower with ladders that can be placed next to a wall and allow soldiers to get over the wall and into the city.

18.note: Alternate translation: [He did something even worse than that: he reached out]

18.q: reached out with his hand to make a promise
18.note: This refers to taking hold of another person’s hand as a sign of friendship and agreement. Here it represents the covenant oath that he made with the king of Babylon.

19.q: was it not my oath that he despised and my covenant that he broke?
19.note: Yahweh asks this leading question to emphasize the affirmative answer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this question as a statement. Alternate translation: [it was my oath that the king of Jerusalem despised and my covenant that he broke.]

19.q: I will bring his punishment on his head
19.note: The idiom “bring … on his head” means that he will experience this punishment. See how you translated this idiom in Ezekiel 11:21. Alternate translation: [I will cause him to suffer his punishment]

20.q: I will spread my net out over him, and he will be caught in my hunting net
20.note: Yahweh speaks of enabling the enemy army to capture the king as if he were trapping the king in a net.

20.q: he will be caught in my hunting net
20.note: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: [I will catch him in my hunting net]

21.q: All of his refugees … armies will fall by the sword
21.note: The word “fall” is a euphemism for “die.” Here the word “sword” is a metonym for soldiers who kill people with swords. Alternate translation: [Soldiers will kill all his refugees … armies]

21.q: the ones who remain will be scattered in every direction
21.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones who remain alive will flee in every direction] or [the enemy soldiers will scatter in every directions the ones who remain alive]

When Yahweh says that people will know that he is Yahweh, he is implying that they will know that he is the one true God who has supreme authority and power. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 6:7. Alternate translation: [understand that I am Yahweh, the one true God] or [realize that I, Yahweh, have supreme power and authority]

22.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh resumes the parable that he had told in [Ezekiel 17:1](ta:17) and speaks about Jerusalem as if it were a branch that he plants on the mountains of Israel.

24.q: Then all the trees of the field will know that I am Yahweh
24.note: Yahweh speaks of trees as if they are people who can know about him. The trees represent the nations and the people who live in them. (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

24.q: I bring down the high trees and I raise up the low trees
24.note: Alternate translation: [I cut down the tall trees and I cause the little trees to grow]
when a plant dries up and dies.
